original.description: The InCubed Element of the European Earth Watch Programme (InCubed) aims at accompanying the European economic operators in the Earth Observation market rapid evolution currently witnessed in Europe and overseas. InCubed offers a new process in ESA Earth Observation programmes to strengthen and stimulate the realization of endeavours near-to-the-market with Economic Operators. Activities to be supported include the development and/or demonstration of space assets (missions, instruments, prototype element of EO constellation), innovative mission management solution, including for future EO constellation, the development of application platforms, etc. InCubed is looking for commercial viability by the end of the activity (up to at least a minimum viable product level) and a substantial degree of innovation i.e. adding new value to the EO commercial landscape. Commercial customer engagement/involvement is mandatory. Commercial customers are encouraged to be either as part of the consortium representing the value chain or as beta testers/validators of the developed product/service.  Customer engagement/involvement must be highlighted at the pitch and proposal stage. Letters of potential customer support/interest are seen as a very positive aspect. The actual scope of the proposed activities is defined by the economic operators themselves in relevance to the InCubed objectives. Two development cycles are possible within InCubed: TheDe-Risking Cycle (start TRL 4) and Product Development Cycle (startTRL 6) depending on the maturity of the concept being developed. Regarding this forthcoming Announcement of Partnership Opportunity, Economic operators are invited to register and submit idea pitches onto ideas.esa.int (InCubed channel). Following a positive pitch meeting, the second step is to fill in a Part 1 (Outline) proposal template, which must be supported by the Participating State(s) having jurisdiction over them. Following a positive assessment,the economic operators will be invited to submit a Part 2 (Full) proposal template, as per established procedure and evaluation criteria. The proposals to be supported by InCubed will have to be co-funded by the economic operators (partnership agreements), as a sign of their engagement and belief in their own business case.

original.description: Under NAVISP Element 3, the Agency issues this Call for Proposals for the development of initiatives in the Position, Navigation and Timing domain. Element 3 is focused on participating States' priorities and aims at supporting their national navigation activities along the whole value chain. Element 3 configures as an ad-hoc support element, which is envisaged per country and possibly per domain, for the development and promotion of products, applications and services based on GNSS and more widely on PNT systems. Following participating states request, ESA may provide technical assistance in various areas. Element 3 configures as an opportunity for the participating States delegations to animate and coordinate discussions with national entities and to set up the processes to identify and federate institutional demands. This will foster cooperation as well as possible national partnerships with a wide diversity of actors, enlarging the national space community (agency, industries, universities, and research centres) and strengthening its relationships with authorities, organisations, institutions, industries, and research actors from non-space sectors. Industry and research institutes of Participant States are encouraged to contact the NAVISP Element 3 team to discuss the development of activities of national relevance and matching institutional interests. Details on the tendering process and preparing the Full Proposal are provided in the Standard Call for Proposals.

original.description: The Luxembourg's National Programme - LuxIMPULSE Programme, aims to strengthen worldwide competitiveness of Luxembourg industry in the near term in existing markets and to establish strategic capabilities which will result in stronger competitiveness in the medium term on existing or new markets, and to support the implementation of Luxembourg national priorities.The Call for Proposals is addressed only to economic operators - be it as Prime or Subcontractor level - registered in Luxembourg, unless otherwise instructed and approved by the Luxembourg Space Agency. The proposed work shall not overlap with any currently running ESA Contract awarded to any entity in the proposal consortium.Activities submitted in the frame of LuxIMPULSE Programme may be related to the study, improvement or development of space systems, subsystems, technology, ground systems for space applications, or downstream service products based on space data.It must be noted that according to the Procurement Regulations ESA/REG/001 rev. 5, Art. 18, Tenderers areeligible to participate in a tendering procedure of the Agency provided they possess the necessary professional and technical qualifications, professional and technical competences, financial resources, equipment and other physical facilities, managerial capability, reliability, experience and the personnel, to perform a Contract.The support to the activity by the Luxembourg Space Agency is mandatory. The activities selected will be funded by the Agency at a level depending on the nature of the economic operator and the maturity and proximity to market of the activity. The remainder will be funded by the economic operator's internal own resources and shall not include any additional source of public funding. The economic operator's contribution can be either monetary or in-kind.

Introduction 

FuturEnergy Ireland is a leading Irish wind developer established in 2021 as a stand-alone joint venture between Coillte and ESB. The company was formed with an aim to maximise the potential of Ireland’s unique wind and land resources and accelerate Ireland’s transformation to a low carbon energy economy.  FuturEnergy Ireland is targeting the development of 1GW of renewable energy by 2030 through the advancement of high-quality onshore wind and battery storage projects. These projects would power an estimated 730,000 homes annually, make a significant contribution to Ireland’s commitment to produce 80% of electricity from renewable sources by the end of this decade, and deliver material emissions reductions.  


Contract for service – Invitation to tender

(a) Introduction
FuturEnergy Ireland is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified and experienced panel of Contractors to undertake LiDAR topographical survey services as required. The survey is
intended to provide accurate and reliable terrain, surface, imagery and survey-control data to support project development, design and related technical activities.
The successful Contractors will be responsible for all necessary planning, permissions, survey control, data acquisition, processing, independent validation, reporting and final deliverables.
Candidates should note that the objective of this tender competition is twofold: A) to appoint successful firms to the panel, and B) to award an initial assignment which relates to Project 1 located in Co Laois detailed in Appendix 5 of this document. 
Tenderers should note that four further projects are expected to be awarded through the panel shortly after it is established. These projects are not exhaustive, and additional projects will be awarded through the panel during its term, subject to project requirements and the Contracting Entity’s discretion.

(b) Objectives
The appointed Contractors shall:
Undertake a complete LiDAR high-resolution aerial imagery survey of the specified survey area.
Establish robust survey control and independent validation checkpoints using survey-grade GNSS RTK/PPK methods.
Provide accurate, quality-assured terrain, surface, point-cloud, imagery, contour and survey-control deliverables in the formats specified.
Demonstrate compliance with the required coordinate reference system, accuracy, point-density, validation and reporting requirements.

(c) Scope of Services




1. Survey Planning, Permissions and Mobilisation
The Contractors shall prepare the survey methodology and flight plan, secure all necessary permissions and approvals, coordinate access requirements, identify constraints and confirm the proposed survey programme before mobilisation.

2. Survey Control and Referencing
The survey shall be referenced to the Irish Transverse Mercator (ITM) coordinate system and Malin Head Ordnance Datum (MHOD). Ground control and independent validation checkpoints shall be established using survey-grade GNSS RTK/PPK methods.
A minimum of 20% of survey control points shall be retained as independent checkpoints and shall not be used during processing.


3. LiDAR and Aerial Imagery Acquisition
The Contractors shall acquire LiDAR and high-resolution aerial imagery sufficient to generate accurate Digital Terrain Models, Digital Surface Models, classified point clouds and orthorectified imagery.
The LiDAR system shall provide a minimum of five returns per pulse and shall be capable of reliable ground penetration through dense vegetation and forestry cover.

4. Minimum Technical Requirements
Horizontal accuracy: hard detail, including buildings, walls, roads and other defined features, shall be <= +/-50 mm; soft detail, including vegetation and natural terrain features, shall be <= +/-75 mm.
Vertical accuracy: hard detail and open ground shall be <= +/-75 mm; vegetated and forested areas shall be <= +/-100 mm.
Point density: minimum average LiDAR density of 150 points/m2 and minimum classified ground density of 15 points/m2 beneath forest canopy.
All reported accuracies shall be verified using independent checkpoints not used during processing.

5. Processing, Classification and Quality Assurance
The Contractors shall process, classify and validate the survey data, document the processing workflow, undertake appropriate quality assurance and quality control, and report achieved point density and horizontal and vertical accuracy.

6. Required Deliverables
Raw and classified LiDAR point clouds in LAS/LAZ format.
Digital Terrain Model (DTM) GeoTIFF at 0.25 m resolution.
Digital Surface Model (DSM) GeoTIFF at 0.25 m resolution.
Canopy Height Model (CHM) GeoTIFF at 0.5 m resolution
Orthorectified RGB imagery with a ground sampling distance of 5 cm/pixel or better.
0.5 m contour dataset in ESRI Shapefile and AutoCAD DWG formats. (Optional)
Survey control coordinates and validation results.
Final survey report detailing the survey methodology, equipment, processing workflow, point density, and horizontal and vertical accuracy assessment.




7. Optional Project Photography and Videography
The Contractors may be requested to carry out occasional aerial photography and videography surveys to capture site imagery for communications, publicity, stakeholder engagement, reporting and promotional purposes. All outputs shall be provided in high-resolution digital formats suitable for print and online use.
